name: Lavender Grey
lede: Lavender grey is a pale, cool grey with a trace of purple, named for the color of lavender flowers.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines *lavender* as a pale lilac, the color of lavender flowers, and notes the shades lavender grey and lavender blue [1]. It adds that the word may come from the Latin *lavare*, to wash [1]. The swatch here is a light purplish grey, and the nearest ISCC-NBS name is light purplish gray [2]. Ridgway carried the name over from his 1886 *Nomenclature of Colors* into his 1912 atlas, whose aged plate is only approximate [2]. See [[lavender]], [[lilac]] and [[grey]] for the colors it sits between [2].

St Clair uses a related phrase, lavender-gray-pink, for the dull pinkish hulls of a shipping line's liners, in the story behind [[mountbatten-pink]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 172, 0.72 per cent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 1.3 per cent of paintings from then, 2.2 times the expected rate [4]. Inside a painting it is usually a light, as in 69 per cent of 107 paintings [4]. John Singer Sargent uses it in 8 of the 287 works we hold, 3.1 times the baseline [4]. In Google Books the word peaks in the 1910s [5].
